NEC 314.16 NEC 2020 basis · one governing size prices non-EGC allowances · volume check only
Box Type
Gang — the number of device positions/openings. It is not the number of conductors. RACO multigang rows are exact products with their own catalog capacity, not an "N-gang" formula.
Ring / raised cover
Ring / raised cover — select the actual compatible ring/cover by opening count and raised height. Empire Code uses the verified catalog capacity of that exact product; height alone does not determine added volume — two rings of the same raised height can carry different capacities. Marked ring/cover/extension volume is added per NEC 314.16(A). Not listed? Choose Other / Custom.
Custom extra volume (in³)
Custom extra volume — enter the permitted cubic capacity of the actual ring, cover, or extension when it is not in the catalog. Do not enter its height. Use the volume marked/listed on the product per NEC 314.16(A).
Wire Size (largest, governs allowances)
# Conductors (counted)
# Devices (yokes)
Device yoke — a yoke/strap is the metal mounting strap that supports a switch, receptacle, or similar device. Enter the number of yokes in the box. Each yoke takes a double allowance of the governing wire size: NEC 314.16(B)(4).
Internal Clamps
Internal clamps — count internal cable clamps that occupy box-fill volume. Do not count external connectors as internal clamps. One allowance covers all internal clamps: NEC 314.16(B)(2).
Entering EGCs + bonding jumpers
EGC — Equipment Grounding Conductor. Count equipment grounding conductors and equipment bonding jumpers entering the box. Do not count a grounding pigtail located entirely inside the box. Rule: NEC 314.16(B)(5).

Continuous Portion (A)
NEC Art. 100: a load whose maximum current is expected to continue for 3 hours or more. Sized at 125% per 210.19(A)(1) / 215.2(A)(1).
Circuit Type
Feeds a Dwelling Unit?
NYCEC 215.2(A)(1): a feeder supplying a dwelling unit shall be 3 conductors, minimum 8 AWG Cu or 6 AWG Al.
100%-Rated Assembly
Only Yes if the complete assembly, including the overcurrent device, is listed for continuous operation at 100% of its rating. Rare below 400 A.
